solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fan is something you cast in river

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the river named here

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
you cast a vote at an election

explanation.surface: An angler's riddle: a fan is a fly you cast into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests fishing, but here it is casting a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A devoted follower or enthusiast is a fan, a synonym.

clue.text: Public transport: alternative to a submarine?

definitions.meaning: a bus with two floors of seats
a sandwich with two layers of filling, as opposed to a long sub roll; also a craft that goes up rather than under the water

explanation.surface: Choosing how to travel: take the bus rather than the submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: A submarine is also a long filled roll, so the second sense is a stacked sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-storey bus and a three-slice sandwich both carry this name.

clue.text: What might grow in garden, or in cave, unusually

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the words before it appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Something that might grow in a garden, or oddly in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell, a garden flowering plant, has this botanical genus name.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval at uniform skirt

parts.note: tut is the sound of mild disapproval
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone clicks their tongue at a schoolgirl's uniform skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet dancer's short stiff frilled garment is a kind of skirt.

clue.text: As likely heir, perhaps, led set astray

indicators.note: gone astray means wandered off course, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A likely heir who led his set off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn child is usually the one expected to inherit, hence the hedging perhaps.

clue.text: Cricket side the best ever? That's public knowledge

parts.note: the on side (leg side) is one half of a cricket field
a record is the best performance ever achieved

explanation.surface: A boast that a cricket team is the greatest ever, which everyone knows.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something publicly documented and admitted is known to all, an idiom for public knowledge.

clue.text: Not fleshy, object when having bottom pinched

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, and pinched means stolen, so it goes

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Someone skinny complains when their bottom is pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' reads as a cheeky squeeze but means stolen: the last letter of THING is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean, bony and lacking flesh are all synonyms of the answer.

clue.text: Many held briefly, improperly, in Wilts RAF base

indicators.note: improperly means arranged wrongly, so these letters are reordered
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of held is dropped

explanation.surface: A tale of many people wrongly detained at a military airbase in Wiltshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims held to HEL; 'improperly' rearranges MANY plus HEL. Wilts is short for Wiltshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This Wiltshire village was long home to a Royal Air Force station, an example.

clue.text: Traditional performer: one pulling sledge after car?

indicators.note: after places the sledge-puller following the car in the answer

parts.note: Morris was a British car make, as in the Morris Minor
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A folk performer is pictured hauling a sledge behind a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris was a British car brand; Dancer is one of Father Christmas's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: An English folk dancer with bells and handkerchiefs is a traditional performer, an example.

clue.text: Promoted in the end, you chattered idly

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word you

parts.note: to prate is to chatter idly

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets promoted after a lot of idle chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' looks like an adverb for 'Promoted' but takes the last letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised to a higher rating or grade means much the same as promoted, a synonym.

clue.text: Part for ukelele an orchestra gives girl

indicators.note: part means only a piece of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: An orchestra writes a ukulele part for a girl to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across ukelELE AN ORchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name is a fair definition by the girl's-name convention.

clue.text: Feline, extra large, around New York, returning

indicators.note: returning means the assembled letters are read backwards
around means the clothing size goes round the city

parts.note: XL is the clothing size extra large

explanation.surface: A big cat prowls around New York and comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' and 'returning' sound like the cat's travels; they are the containment and reversal signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-tailed wild cat with tufted ears is a feline, an example.

clue.text: Move up, prior to creating miscellany

indicators.note: move says the letters of the next words are shifted around

explanation.surface: An instruction to shuffle things up before compiling a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of dried petals, or figuratively any medley, is a miscellany.

clue.text: Mostly opposing abortion, I note, having had many children?

indicators.note: mostly means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: pro-life describes opposition to abortion
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A campaigner against abortion who has raised a large family.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitful and producing offspring abundantly; the question mark admits it more usually describes output.

clue.text: Concerned with permit to collect vehicle being suitable

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: to collect means the permit takes the vehicle inside it

parts.note: to let is to permit
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A permit to pick up a vehicle is checked for suitability.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent or apt to the matter in hand; a synonym of suitable.

clue.text: Captivated woman, married, going with our boss at The Times?

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
ED, the editor, runs a newspaper such as The Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is smitten with a married woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ENA is a crossword-favourite woman's name; 'going with' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmed and in love describes someone captivated, a synonym.

clue.text: Venomous snake in scarlet made harsh sounds

indicators.note: in places the snake within the colour

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A poisonous red snake hisses harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Grated, croaked or spoke gratingly; the verb means made harsh sounds.

clue.text: Lay next to a character from Athens

parts.note: to lay money is to bet it

explanation.surface: Someone lies down beside a Greek letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like lie down, but means wager.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet is a character used in Athens.

clue.text: The issue of hoax comes to an end

parts.note: to kid is to hoax or tease
something that dies out comes to an end

explanation.surface: The upshot of a prank finally fizzles out.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in law and old usage means offspring, and these are little children.

clue.text: US detective and British ones upset king

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: American and British detectives fall out with a king.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a private eye or police investigator.

clue.text: Musical note no good — alas for this?

definitions.text: Musical note no good — alas for this?

parts.note: so (soh) is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tune that is no good, sadly, so it went for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nods to 'going for a song': something no good, alas, is sold cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune with words is what goes cheaply in the idiom, the whole clue hinting at it.

clue.text: Uninspiring expert thus penning article

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dull professional writes an equally dull article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull, matter-of-fact and lacking imagination; a synonym of uninspiring.

clue.text: Donor doesn't ever, ice being broken

indicators.note: being broken means the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A donor who never helps break the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives, so the opposite action, accepting, is what a donor doesn't do.

clue.text: Follows sailor, providing a bright night light

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone trails a sailor who carries a lamp at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is so named.
